problem: The applicability selector is constrained with sh:hasValue true, so every targeted ship must assert that the air receivers serve an additional purpose. The requirement is conditional and must allow an explicit false value for ships to which the condition does not apply.
required_change: Require the selector to be present and boolean, but do not constrain it to true; activate the additional-capacity checks only when its value is true.
regression_guard: Preserve ship as the target and preserve true as the activation value for the conditional rule.

location: MainShape / nltl:airReceiverCapacity and nltl:additionalPurposeRequiredAirCapacity property shapes
problem: Both capacity properties have unconditional sh:minCount 1 and sh:maxCount 1 constraints, so they are mandatory for every ship even when nltl:airReceiverServesAdditionalPurpose is false.
required_change: Make the cardinality requirements conditional on nltl:airReceiverServesAdditionalPurpose being true, while retaining the one-value requirement in the active branch.
regression_guard: Do not make either capacity mandatory when the applicability selector is false.

problem: The SPARQL constraint compares raw numericValue literals without requiring a unit for nltl:additionalPurposeRequiredAirCapacity or checking unit compatibility and conversion. Numerically comparing quantities expressed in different units can reverse the sufficiency result.
required_change: Require unit-bearing quantities with compatible volume units and compare normalized values, or explicitly convert both operands to a common unit before applying the less-than test.
regression_guard: Preserve the sufficiency condition that airReceiverCapacity must be at least the additional-purpose required capacity.
